title: Hegseth Medals Tomb Sentinel Who Scolded His Entourage for Arlington Protocol Breach
snippet: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded the Joint Service Commendation Medal to an Army guard who publicly reprimanded his group for laughing near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Veterans Day.
content:
WASHINGTON — Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded a Joint Service Commendation Medal on Thursday to the Army sentinel who publicly reprimanded members of his entourage for chatting and laughing near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery.

The incident occurred on Veterans Day following the annual wreath-laying ceremony. Hegseth, accompanied by his wife Jennifer and three top aides, posed for photographs on the steps overlooking the historic site, which has served as a sacred place of reflection and mourning since 1921. Video captured members of the defense chief's group laughing as they moved up the steps, prompting an immediate reaction from the guard on duty.

A sentinel from the U.S. Army's 3rd Infantry Regiment, widely known as The Old Guard, stepped forward and projected across the plaza: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!"

Footage of the rebuke spread rapidly across social media platforms, leading Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell to issue a public statement backing the guard's conduct. Parnell noted that the soldier "correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum."

Hegseth posted a photograph on Thursday showing him pinning the commendation medal onto the unnamed specialist's chest. "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist," Hegseth wrote on social media. "Carry on Patriots."

Political Storm Clouds Gather at the Pentagon

The episode comes during an intensely turbulent week for the Pentagon chief. On Tuesday, House Republicans managed to maneuver around an impeachment effort against Hegseth, voting to refer articles of impeachment back to the House Judiciary Committee and effectively shelving the effort for the remainder of the current legislative session.

The impeachment resolution, reintroduced by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY), accused Hegseth of committing high crimes and misdemeanors, alleging unauthorized military operations and violations of the War Powers Resolution linked to ongoing military engagements in Iran.

However, Hegseth's reprieve may prove short-lived. Following sweeping gains in the recent midterm elections, Democrats secured a sizable House majority for the upcoming legislative session starting in January 2027. Democratic leadership has already signaled plans to immediately revive proceedings against the Defense Secretary when they assume control of the chamber.
